metadata.title: Swissmedic information sheet: Safety Reporting in clinical trials
metadata.legal_basis: Agency guidance or notice under the Therapeutic Products Act; legislation prevails.
metadata.applicability: Applicants, sponsors and market authorization holders reporting ICSRs (see the PV Info ICSR rulebook for scope).

candidates.statement: 2 Notification of S uspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reactions (SUSARs) in clinical trials of categories B and C (Art. 41 of the Ordinance on Clinical Trials in Human Research (ClinO, SR 810.305) A ll Suspected Unexpected Serious Adverse Reactions ( SUSARs ) , occurring in the framework of clinical trials o f categories B and C at Swiss trial centres, must be reported to Swiss medic . Please note , that all three criteria (serious + related + unexpected based on the R eference S afety I nformation [RSI] ) must be fulfilled for an adverse reaction to qualify as a SUSAR .

Specific information for clinical trials with ATMP s : In clinical trials with ATMPs, relatedness does not only refer to the ATMP itself, but also to interventions associated with it. Therefore, please also submit serious adverse events as SUSARs that are considered related to any of the following aspects:

candidates.statement: ▪ Comparators and placebos administered with in clinical trials are Investigational M e dicinal Products ( IMPs ) (independent of their registration status) . Therefore , SUSARs associated with a comparator product or a placebo follow the same reporting requirements as the test IMP. I n the cases, where SUSARs are realized (after unblinding) to be associated with placebo , the sponsor should report these events and clarify that the causality changed from IMP to placebo .
candidates.context: ▪ S erious events related to an y other ATMP - specific mechanism not covered by the categories above Important: ▪ After initial report of a SUSAR, follow - up reports should only be submitted in case of change to the status of any of the three criteria applicable for the definition of SUSAR (seriousness, relatedness , un expectedness based on the reference safety information) . F ollow - up reports for SUSAR s where the initial status of these three criteria for the definition of SUSAR is unchanged (for ex . update d laboratory values, concomitant medication etc. ) do not need to be submitted .

candidates.context: 4 Annual List of Events and Deficiencies or the Development Safety Update Report (Art. 43 para. 1 ClinO) for clinical trials of categories B and C (Art. 43 para. 3 ClinO) The Annual List of Events and Deficiencies or the Development Safety Update Report (DSUR) are summar ies of the current status of knowledge of the clinical investigation or of the development program with the specific IMP and describe the general progress of the clinical trial and new safety issues, identified and potential risks of active substances/medicinal products during clinical trials that could have an impact on the protection of clinical trial participants (Art. 43 para. 1 ClinO) . Separate DSURs or Annual List of Events and Deficiencies have to be submitted for each IMP.

candidates.statement: In accordance with Art. 43, par. 3, ClinO, th e Annual List of Events and Deficiencies or DSUR must be submitted to Swissmedic for every clinical trial of categories B and C carried out in Switzerland.
candidates.context: Alternatively, one Annual List of Events and Deficiencies or DSUR focusing on the combination treatment can be submitted instead . Trial - specific safety and progress reports can be submitted as well, where the safety updates about the trial are summarized (used in case the sponsor is not the manufacturer of the IMP ) . I nformation about the general progress of the clinical trial has to be submitted yearly, either together with the Annual List of Events and Deficiencies (or DSUR ) or in a separate submission . The information required is listed in chapter “Trial Progress” of the template “Annual Safety and General Progress Trial Report” available on the website of Swissethics swissethics.ch/en/templates/meldungen . candidates.statement: I nformation about the general progress of the clinical trial has to be submitted yearly, either together with the Annual List of Events and Deficiencies (or DSUR ) or in a separate submission . The information required is listed in chapter “Trial Progress” of the template “Annual Safety and General Progress Trial Report” available on the website of Swissethics swissethics.ch/en/templates/meldungen . These data can either be submitted using the Swissethics template or provided as a separate document The Annual List of Events and Deficiencies or DSUR as well as the general progress of the clinical trial is submitted once a year, from the date of study approval in Switzerland and throughout the duration of the clinical trial in Switzerland . T he last Annual List of Events and Deficiencies or DSUR as well as the last general progress of the clinical trial to be submitted must cover the Last Patient Last Visit (LPLV) in Switzerland for that specific trial . There is no need for further submissions after LPLV since the information on safety will be captured in the clinical study report.
candidates.context: In accordance with Art. 43, par. 3, ClinO, th e Annual List of Events and Deficiencies or DSUR must be submitted to Swissmedic for every clinical trial of categories B and C carried out in Switzerland. The following details must be included in the Annual List of Events and Deficiencies or DSUR : report n umber (consecutive numbering), product name, clinical trial code , time period covered by the report, date of the report, list of events or adverse reactions (including SUSARs) , name and address of the sponsor.
